Maya (support): FYI customer AcmeInc opened a high-severity ticket — p99 spike to ~3.2s after yesterday's runtime deploy. They say it started ~10:45 UTC. They included example request IDs.
Maya (support): Ticket excerpt: "After the deploy our interactive completions p99 jumped from 650ms to ~3s for short prompts. This is blocking our UI."
Jenna (customer-success): I validated with the account — they reproduced against our hosted API, not a private deploy. They sent logs: request ids r-12a3, r-12a7, r-12b0.
Maya (support): Copying logs snippet we received:
```
[2026-03-16T10:47:11Z] r-12a3 tenant=acme prompt_len=12 latency=3204ms route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=120 max_batch=64
[2026-03-16T10:48:02Z] r-12a7 tenant=acme prompt_len=8 latency=3120ms route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=120 queue_len=1
[2026-03-16T10:49:05Z] r-12b0 tenant=acme prompt_len=5 latency=2987ms route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=120
```
Raj (eng-sre): Thanks. That looks like requests are hitting continuous-batcher with a high hold window. Any deploy changed batcher defaults?
Maya (support): Deploy note mentions "tweak: reduce batching latency by increasing hold window for throughput" — so yes, defaults were bumped to 120ms global.
Eli (oncall): Oof. Increasing global hold helps throughput but can blow up p99 on tiny prompts. We should check per-tenant overrides and fastpath.
Raj (eng-sre): Quick checks I ran: cluster metrics show microburst of small requests from Acme at 10:45, median tokens per request=14, 90th=30. Batcher config now: 
```
{
  "continuous_batcher": {
    "max_hold_ms": 120,
    "max_batch_size": 64,
    "min_coalesce": 2
  }
}
```
Raj (eng-sre): The combination (120ms + large batch size) is expected to create high p99 for small prompts when traffic is spiky. Suggest immediate mitigation: roll back max_hold_ms to 30ms for hosted default and enable tenant bypass for small synchronous requests.
Jenna (customer-success): Acme needs a hotfix ASAP. Can we do a targeted per-tenant override instead of global rollback?
Eli (oncall): We can push a per-tenant override to set max_hold_ms=20 for Acme. That's quick and low risk. I'll prepare a canary.
Maya (support): Customer approval requested — they agreed to a per-tenant override.
Raj (eng-sre): Operational steps (quick):
1) run: `redwoodctl config apply --tenant acme --patch '{"continuous_batcher.max_hold_ms":20}'`
2) watch p99 on tenant: `metrics query tenant_latency{tenant="acme",quantile="p99"}`
3) if p99 improves in 5m, schedule global rollback of default to 30ms in next maintenance window.
Eli (oncall): I'll execute step 1 now on the canary cluster and tail logs.
deploy-bot: deploy started by Eli (oncall) at 2026-03-16T11:02:10Z - patch id cfg-8891
Eli (oncall): Patch applied to 3 nodes. Observing latency...
Raj (eng-sre): Early numbers: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 380ms, p99 for Acme dropped from ~3s to ~650ms within 90s.
Maya (support): Passed on to customer: they confirm UI responsiveness improved.
Jenna (customer-success): Customer asked for root cause notes for the postmortem: they want explanation of tradeoffs (batch size vs hold window) and recommended safe defaults for interactive UIs.
Raj (eng-sre): Addendum we should send in postmortem: When global hold window is increased to favor throughput, small-sized prompt workloads will see more queuing with single-request queues waiting up to max_hold_ms to assemble larger batches. For workloads with low prompt length or synchronous UX, smaller hold windows or bypass fastpath are necessary.
Maya (support): Next actions: (a) file incident ticket with RCA draft, (b) schedule global default rollback to 30ms and limit max_batch_size to 32 for streaming endpoints, (c) add an automatic per-tenant detector to reduce hold window when 95% of requests < 40 tokens.
Eli (oncall): I'll open the incident and schedule the rollback. Assigning to Raj for config changes and to DevEx to add the detector alert.
Raj (eng-sre): Quick repro steps for engineering doc: run 1000 parallel tiny requests (prompt len 5-20) with hold window 120ms vs 30ms and compare p99. Example load command:
```
hey -n 1000 -c 200 "POST /v1/complete" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}'
```
Maya (support): Thanks team. I'll update the ticket and mark as mitigated once rollback scheduled.
Jenna (customer-success): Customer asked whether billing/cost will be affected — please note throughput will drop slightly, we'll advise on quota/cost tradeoff.
Raj (eng-sre): Noted. We'll include expected token/sec delta in the postmortem.
Eli (oncall): Closing loop: monitor for 24h post-rollback; if we see increased latency elsewhere, we'll revisit adaptive per-tenant hold window feature. :thumbsup:
Maya (support): Closing this thread for now — followup in incident ticket INC-2026-114.
